entries.claim: This setting prints the 18-word secreta proper w001–w018, followed by the separate literal cue “Per Dóminum.” The supplied complete conclusion and Amen are not printed at this proper locus.

locator.section: RG115a; complete supplied conclusion w019–w039 and Amen w040 only; accented common words and terminal; proper body excluded

entries.claim: This setting’s RG115a supplies the complete Father-directed Per Dominum ending w019–w039 and Amen w040, excluding the proper body. The literal rubric list is unaccented. The matching common words on p.123 and terminal on p.226 control selected stress; p.226 also distinguishes the Amen response period. These controls do not establish response actors, singing or the distribution of conclusions in grouped orations.

entries.claim: This setting prints the 18-word secreta proper w001–w018, followed by the separate literal cue “Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte.” The supplied complete conclusion and Amen are not printed at this proper locus. This is a separately set witness of the same received tradition, not proof of independent historical transmission.

locator.section: RG115a; this setting’s supplied conclusion w019–w039 and Amen w040 only; proper body excluded

entries.claim: This setting’s own RG115a supplies its complete ending and Amen w019–w040, excluding the proper body. Literal accents, punctuation and the Amen list semicolon remain in the transcript. Formula wording alone does not establish actors, singing, participation or grouped-orations conclusion distribution.
